title: Number of Distinct Binary Strings After Applying Operations
summary: Given a binary string s and a positive integer k , you can perform the following operation any number of times: - Choose any substring of size k from s and flip all its characters, turning 1's into 0's and 0's into 1's.
statement: Given a binary string s and a positive integer k , you can perform the following operation any number of times: - Choose any substring of size k from s and flip all its characters, turning 1's into 0's and 0's into 1's. Return the number of distinct binary strings that can be obtained. Since the result can be large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7 . Note that: - A binary string consists only of the characters 0 and 1. - A substring is a contiguous part of the string.
constraints: An operation flips every bit in any contiguous substring of length k.
Apply operations any number of times and count distinct binary strings reachable from s.
hints: There are n-k+1 possible starting positions for a length-k flip.
Each window is either flipped an odd number of times or an even number, giving a binary choice.
The flip vectors are linearly independent because each has a unique leftmost position not present in later vectors.
Therefore all 2^(n-k+1) parity selections produce distinct reachable strings.
editorial: Therefore all 2^(n-k+1) parity selections produce distinct reachable strings.

tests.explanation: There are two possible length-three windows, and independently choosing whether to flip each produces four distinct strings.
The sole bit can be flipped or left unchanged, so two strings are reachable.
